proposal.utterance: Classify 'a property status' in BFO terms.

entities.label: PropertyStatus
entities.rationale: A property status (e.g., 'owned', 'encumbered', 'mortgaged', 'fee simple') is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a material entity (the property/parcel) or in a legal person bearing property rights. It is a Quality because it is a measurable, determinate characteristic of the bearer at a time — not a disposition or role. It is not a Role because property status is not externally grounded in a social function assigned by others in the same sense; rather, it is a relational quality that tracks the legal standing of the entity with respect to ownership and encumbrance. BFO_0000019 (Quality) is the best fit. It could alternatively be modeled as a Role (BFO_0000023) if the emphasis is on the socially-conferred, externally-assigned character of legal property standing — this is flagged as an open question.

relations.rationale: PropertyStatus is classified as a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019) because it is a specifically dependent continuant inhering in a bearer (a legal person or parcel of land) and characterizing that bearer's standing with respect to ownership, encumbrance, or other property-related attributes at a time.

open_questions: Should 'property status' be typed as Quality (BFO_0000019) — emphasizing it as a measurable, time-indexed characteristic of the bearer — or as Role (BFO_0000023) — emphasizing that it is socially and legally conferred by an external recognition system (e.g., a title registry, court judgment)?
What is the intended bearer of this property status: a physical parcel (material entity, BFO_0000040), a legal person (an individual bearing a role), or both?
Is 'property status' meant to cover only legal property (land, chattels) or also abstract property (intellectual property rights)? The latter might require a different bearer type.
Should this class be linked to existing classes such as working:LegalRight or working:InstitutionalRecognitionQuality as a parent or sibling?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'a property status' most naturally denotes the specific legal standing of an entity (person or parcel) with respect to ownership, title, or encumbrance — e.g., 'fee simple owner', 'lessee', 'mortgagee'. In BFO 2020, this is best captured as a Quality (BFO_0000019): a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer and characterizes it at a time. It is not a process (it persists rather than unfolds), not a generically dependent continuant (it is not a copyable pattern), and not a material entity. The main ambiguity is whether the socially-conferred, institutionally-recognized character of property status pushes it toward Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally grounded. A Role typing would be defensible if the emphasis is on the social-institutional conferral. The proposed classification as Quality is conservative and standard for legal status attributes; the open questions flag the Role alternative for the user to decide.
